newsitem.title: USA: Montanta winter wheat seeding nears completion.
newsitem.headline: Montanta winter wheat seeding nears completion.

text.p: Winter wheat seeding neared completion and producers were in their final stages of row crop harvest in the week ended Oct 20, Montana's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.

Winter wheat was 95 percent planted against 88 percent a week earlier, last year's 94 percent and the average of 88 percent. Wheat had emerged on 61 percent of the acreage, up from 43 a week earlier and ahead of the 59 percent average.
The report said some welcome moisture came in some areas of the state, with much of it coming as snow.
Topsoil moisture was rated 13 percent very short, 53 percent short, 34 percent adequate and nil surplus.
The sugar beet harvest also made excellent progress, with 91 percent of acreage harvested against 57 percent a week earlier, 76 percent last year and 71 percent average.

Pasture and range feed condition hovered around the prior week's levels, with six percent rated very poor, 33 percent poor, 36 percent fair, 24 percent good and one percent excellent. By the weekend, 61 percent of the cattle and calves were moved off summer ranges. There was a report of pneumonia and pinkeye being a problem due to the dusty conditions in the central district.
